explanation: In Spain, showing the soles of your feet is considered disrespectful because feet are seen as dirty and lowly. This gesture can be interpreted as a sign of contempt or disregard, especially in social or formal settings.
local_tip: Always keep your feet flat on the floor or crossed at the ankles, and avoid pointing your soles toward anyone.
regional_note: This norm is consistent across mainland Spain, though in the Canary Islands and some coastal areas, casual settings may be slightly more relaxed.

also_check.note: The feet are considered the lowest and most impure part of the body; pointing them at someone is a grave insult.
Generally not a major issue, but putting feet on furniture or pointing soles at others can be seen as rude or overly casual.
Showing the soles of your feet is highly offensive, as feet are considered unclean in Arab culture.
